cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the route you thought through is being walked by others.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Start the next piece of work from the edge where the last one ended — a first paragraph, a first shelf, a first meeting, made with your own hands.
cells.core:
Someone gets across because you thought it through ahead of them. The careful work happens before anyone asks, and what reaches them feels like clear ground. Running well, this stays generous — the effort serves their arrival, and you're content to have worked it out rather than to be on display.

What faces you now is completion, and completing means the cleared ground gets built on. A route you've finished doesn't want another pass over it. Begin the next thing from the edge where the old one stopped. The building is what closes the loop — no more walking a path you've walked enough.
cells.sheetLine: What you've worked out is finished enough to stand on.
cells.verb: Charting a way across for someone who can't yet see it
cells.place: Where what's finished is let go of and something new gets to start

cells.tense: You will be checking the path for stones no one else has stepped near.
cells.act: release the method, not the purpose
cells.ask: Catch one way you've been putting the point across that no longer works, and set the phrasing down while keeping the point itself.
cells.core:
The route keeps being corrected past the point anyone needed it corrected. From inside, that reads as care. From the other side, it reads as being handed corrections instead of the point, and people start waiting to be told the right version rather than speaking their own. The aim gets buried under the method.

If you want someone to arrive at the thing themselves, then a phrasing you've outgrown costs the aim nothing. It only costs you the comfort of having worded it right. Say the thing once, plainly. Let them do what they do with it. The point still lands. The method is what's being kept alive, and the method is what's tiring them.
cells.sheetLine: You're still correcting a path they already walk.
cells.verb: Charting a way across for someone who can't yet see it

cells.tense: You were the one who saw the way, and the saying of it has stopped.
cells.act: return the small thing you owe before anyone asks
cells.ask: Think of a reply, an object, a yes or a no that belongs to somebody and has sat with you — hand it over, unprompted.
cells.core:
There was a passage you used to make clear for people, and you've stopped offering it. What you knew didn't leave. It just hasn't been handed across lately. What's left is the standing-still: the way is plain in your head, nobody else has been told, and the door you're at is behind you rather than ahead.

The way forward doesn't run through the old role. It runs through one debt small enough to settle today — no speech about what you used to know, no route laid out for a group. Give back what's owed. That act does what a grand gesture can't: it puts the first plank where the bridge stopped, and the crossing resumes from there.
cells.sheetLine: You knew the way and stopped saying it out loud.
cells.verb: Charting a way across for someone who can't yet see it

cells.tense: The direction is being given by your hand, and you'd say you're not giving it.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Bring a piece of work you're carrying to somebody and settle its next step together before you move on it — not after.
cells.core:
Those near you find their bearings because you've gone ahead and made the ground walkable, and if asked you'd say it's just the obvious thing. The leading is real — private thinking turned outward — and it carries an author who isn't named. The ones being guided sense a hand on the tiller and get told it's only the current.

What shifts this isn't a bigger claim. It's a smaller one. Choose one thing and set its next move with someone rather than for them — a decision reached together, not announced. The direction stops being something you hold alone and becomes something two of you carry. Then it's recognisably yours without needing to be owned.

attempts.check: The draft's one unsupported claim is that the person is actively steering others toward a completion that no longer needs steering — the record shows the signature's shape and balance, not the particulars of this life. A reader could reasonably say the directing has already stopped, or never served others in the first place. The asks survive being wrong because each is one act on the person's own material, done whether or not the reading fits, and teaches them something either way. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that makes the boat, the passage or the vessel sound like a fact of their life rather than a shape the record draws; all four cells keep the shape and drop the fact.
